essential: Boston left the mind supple but formless. Women taught only domestic virtues; 'The garden of Eden was hardly more primitive.'

Blackguard Boston and the snowball war on the Common. Bully Hig is struck by a stone. Henry stays only because his brother Charles is too big to run. Conky Daniels sweeps past those who stand. The moral: blackguards not so black. Then the retrospective line on Savage and Marvin.
Violence familiar from mobs, Garrison, Phillips, Parker, and the Fugitive Slave Law. The bayonets in Court Square wrought 'frenzy' in the fifteen-year-old.

The May 1850 journey to the bedridden Madam. Keep the English railway carriage as a hint of corruption he rather liked. The remembered journey matters more than the actual one. The shock of a slave State's raggedness is 'what slavery caused.'
Washington as unfinished village: the catalpas, the Greek temples image, the marble shaft he walked to before breakfast, the aunt's dry remark.
Doubled response: slavery a crime, yet the South's looseness 'soothed his Johnson blood.' He was not sure he preferred Boston.
The Senate as a friendly club of a Roman species, with Clay, Webster, and Calhoun present. Southern pomposity was genial; he felt more at home than in Boston State House.
President Taylor and Old Whitey; the boy 'half thought he owned' the White House. Presidents were a matter of course in the family.

The road to Mount Vernon: bad roads mean bad morals, yet Washington stands at the end. 'George Washington stood alone,' his Pole Star; Mount Vernon was 'only Quincy in a Southern setting.' The father did not preach.
Return to Boston more political and seventeenth-century in tone; a first sense of party machinery.

The 1851 coalition: Free Soil managers (Wilson, Alley) bargain with the Democrats. The statesmen disdain it yet profit, with Sumner made Senator and Boutwell Governor. The boy's motive was personal; the outcome was lasting moral confusion. 'Tammany Hall stood at the end of the vista.'

The gallery and the 'one-eyed abolitionist' mishearing; the April 24, 1851 vote; running home to tell Sumner, 'the proudest moment in the life of either.' The white ribbon against black crepe, and later doubt about which symbol was correct. Close with exile from Boston, the Cunard smoke, the reasonableness of not going West, and stood 'nearer the year 1 than to the year 1900.'
optional: Henry Higginson's nickname can be dropped if the stone injury stays.
The detailed rail and steamboat itinerary (Trenton, Philadelphia, Chester, Havre de Grace, Baltimore), keeping the remark that memory is all that matters.
The Vice-President's chair/Chief Justice note and the codfish in the House.
Nathaniel Gorham as a third President-equivalent.
The Peter Harveys and Thurlow Weeds sentence, reduced to 'subordinates ran the machine.'
The 'one-ideaed' versus 'one-eyed' clarification can be shortened but not cut alone; it explains the mishearing.
Para 17's West argument can be condensed to two sentences.
risks: Paragraph 4 is very long. Excerpting it risks losing the 'memory, not actual journey' qualification.

title: WASHINGTON (1850-1854)

verbatim.purpose: Retrospective, chilling payoff of the snowball fight.
verbatim.text: he wondered whether their education on Boston Common had taught Savage and Marvin how to die.
like white Greek temples in the abandoned gravel-pits of a deserted Syrian city.
Even at twelve years old he could see his own nature no more clearly than he would at twelve hundred, if by accident he should happen to live so long.
Slavery was wicked, and slavery was the cause of this road's badness which amounted to social crime--and yet, at the end of the road and product of the crime stood Mount Vernon and George Washington.
the faculty of ignoring them makes the practical man; but any attempt to deal with them seriously as education is fatal.

verbatim.purpose: Epigram of the first practical political lesson.
verbatim.text: he learned the nature of a flagrantly corrupt political bargain in which he was too good to take part, but not too good to take profit.

verbatim.purpose: Self-indictment that carries the moral confusion forward.
verbatim.text: As a politician, he was already corrupt, and he never could see how any practical politician could be less corrupt than himself.
Speaking as an American of 1900, he had as yet no education at all. He knew not even where or how to begin.

voice_profile: Third-person autobiography in which the aged author calls his younger self 'he,' 'the boy,' or 'Henry Adams.' It moves between the child's limited view and the old man's retrospective irony. It relies on aphorism and paradox, such as 'Summer was the multiplicity of nature; winter was school.' Self-deprecation is played as mock-scientific analysis: variation, type, force, stamp. Long periodic sentences end in a dry reversal. Lists build through dashes and semicolons. Exact dates anchor the account. Qualifiers like 'perhaps,' 'probably,' and 'he could never decide' recur. Every episode is measured as a lesson in education that taught little or the wrong thing. Double hyphens are characteristic and must be kept.
